Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the run-through earlier — the demo and discussion were helpful. As we discussed, the team is very interested in Redwood but we need a clear Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that maps milestones, owners, and any dependencies so we can get internal buy-in (security, procurement, and engineering).

For the MAP we care most about the "Integration build plan" milestone — specifically: SDK integration for server-side requests, streaming responses for our real-time feature, tool-calling support (we have a scheduling service we'd like Redwood to call), and structured outputs (JSON schema enforcement). Can you draft a MAP that includes owners, target completion dates, and blockers?

Also: target close for procurement is end of Q1 (2026-03-31). If we can show a clear integration timeline that lands before then, that will help.

Appreciate a draft we can circulate to engineering/security.

Thanks,
Sarah Miller
Head of Product, FinApps

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Per our call, please find attached a draft MAP (MAP_v1.2.pdf) focused on the Integration Build Plan milestone. High level summary below; full milestone table is in the attachment.

Integration Build Plan (high level)
- Objective: Enable FinApps to integrate Redwood for real-time user-facing features with reliable streaming and structured outputs.
- Target close (deal): 2026-03-31 (FinApps procurement target)

Key milestones (owners & targets)
1) SDK integration (server-side) — Owner: Dev Patel (Solutions Eng) — Target: 2026-03-10
   - Deliverable: SDK integration guide, example repo, auth setup, perf guidance
   - Dependencies: API keys, network allowlist, test account

2) Streaming integration (low-latency responses) — Owner: Soojin Lee (Infra SE) — Target: 2026-03-15
   - Deliverable: streaming SDK snippet, sample NPM/Py client, SLOs for latency
   - Dependencies: ingress routing, region pinning, TLS certs

3) Tool calling (scheduling service integration) — Owner: Soojin Lee — Target: 2026-03-18
   - Deliverable: tool-calling guide, example webhook, retry/backoff patterns
   - Dependencies: webhook endpoints, auth token rotation policy

4) Structured outputs & schema enforcement — Owner: Aditya Rao (ML Integrations) — Target: 2026-03-12
   - Deliverable: JSON schema templates, runtime validation approach, fallback behavior
   - Dependencies: example prompt templates, eval set for regressions

5) Canary & QA deploys (internal + FinApps) — Owner: Marissa Cole (AE) & Dev Patel — Target: 2026-03-22
   - Deliverable: canary rollout plan, smoke tests, rollback criteria

Next steps
- Dev/SWEs to confirm access and network requirements by 2026-02-27 (Dev Patel)
- SEs to provide integration snippets and example repos by milestone dates
- Security: we'll submit an evidence bundle (SOC2, data flow diagrams) — expect by 2026-02-26

I've attached MAP_v1.2.pdf with the milestone table and an appendix listing dependencies and required FinApps artifacts. Please review and let me know edits — happy to run through with engineering/security next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: MAP_v1.2.pdf
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-02-24T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP Draft: Integration Build Plan — technical clarifications + SOW

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the draft — a few technical clarifications so the MAP is actionable for engineering:

1) SDK integration: we'll provide server-side SDKs for Node/Python; integration will require FinApps to provide a test API key and an IP range to allowlist (or set up mTLS). If FinApps wants on-prem or private deployment we'll need to scope network topology and pricing.

2) Streaming: streaming SLOs depend on region and payload sizes. For the PoC we can commit to 95th percentile token latency of <150ms in us-west for payloads under 1KB; we'll call this out in the SOW. Need FinApps to confirm typical sequence lengths.

3) Tool calling: to integrate with your scheduling service we'll need a webhook endpoint with TLS and a token we can rotate. Also clarifying retry semantics — we'll follow standard exponential backoff up to 3 retries unless you prefer a different policy.

4) Structured outputs: need example schemas (e.g., appointment object), and a small eval set to validate schema conformance. We'll include runtime validation hooks and a fallback slot for human review if parsing fails.

I've attached a short SOW (Integration_SOW.xlsx) with proposed milestones and acceptance criteria — please review.

Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Integration_SOW.xlsx

- For streaming SLOs: can you confirm the 95th percentile <150ms applies to end-to-end time (Redwood processing + network)? We need that for our SLA section.

If you can update the MAP with those two items I'll share with our security and procurement teams. Our internal target is to sign by 2026-03-31 assuming no major blockers.

Appreciate it —
Sarah
